payload.title: Scope usage identity aliases to their backend and provider
payload.summary: P2: collection.reconcile builds thread/turn and invocation/thread alias indexes from unqualified strings, then prefixes backend/provider only after the alias lookup. An unrelated provider using the same thread name changes provider-A from valid to conflicting; the same invocation label under two providers can exclude both valid invocations. Public normalized UsageObservation/storage/report callers are affected. Existing native usage CLI primarily observes Codex/OpenAI, so no live mixed-provider accounting incident, billing error or execution-budget bypass is established.
payload.benefit: Acceptance: through public report and save/load, provider-A alone and provider-A plus unrelated provider-B preserve identical A consumption. Cover reused thread labels with distinct turns and reused invocation labels with distinct threads, unknown-turn aliasing, within-provider legitimate duplicates/ambiguity, attributions and deterministic ordering. Preserve honest unknown categories and within-provider conflicts. Namespace all provider-local alias maps before correspondence, using the existing identity owner, not a new ledger or identity hierarchy.
payload.uncertainty: Independent deterministic temporary metadata reproduction; no model execution, actual subscription/billing claim, automatic approval or repair in this audit.
